topicName: Test Planning, Estimation Techniques, and Test Strategy
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Comprehensive Guide to Test Planning, Estimation Techniques, and Test Strategy in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"A successful manual testing lifecycle relies heavily on meticulous planning, accurate estimation, and a well-defined test strategy. Without these core elements, projects often suffer from missed deadlines, budget overruns, and undetected critical defects."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Test Strategy"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Test Strategy is a high-level document, usually derived from the Business Requirement Specification (BRS) or Project Plan. It outlines the testing approach for the entire organization or a specific project. It is typically static and rarely changes during the project lifecycle."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scope and Objectives: Defines what will be tested and what will not be tested."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Testing Types: Specifies the levels of testing to be performed (e.g., Smoke, Sanity, Functional, Integration, Regression, UAT)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Tools and Environment: Identifies test management tools (e.g., Jira, TestRail) and required test environments."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Risks and Mitigation: Outlines potential testing risks and contingency plans."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Test Planning"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Test Plan is a dynamic document that describes the scope, approach, resources, and schedule of intended testing activities. It is derived from the Test Strategy and Product Description. It answers the questions: What to test? How to test? When to test? Who will test?"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test Plan Identifier & Introduction"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Features to be Tested and Not to be Tested"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test Environment and Test Deliverables"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Schedule, Milestones, and Resource Allocation"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Entry and Exit Criteria (Definition of Ready and Definition of Done)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Entry and Exit Criteria Example"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Setting clear entry and exit criteria ensures quality gates are maintained throughout the manual testing process."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"Entry Criteria (When to start testing):
- Requirements signed off and understood.
- Test cases written and reviewed.
- Build deployed successfully to the Test Environment.

Exit Criteria (When to stop testing):
- 100% execution of high-priority test cases.
- Zero Critical or Blockers open.
- Sign-off obtained from QA Lead / Project Manager."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Test Estimation Techniques"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Test estimation is the process of approximating the time and effort required to complete all testing tasks. Accurate estimation helps project managers allocate resources effectively."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Work Breakdown Structure (WBS): Deconstructs the testing project into smaller, manageable tasks, estimating effort for each component."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Three-Point Estimating (PERT): Calculates an expected duration using Optimistic (O), Most Likely (M), and Pessimistic (P) estimates. Formula: E = (O + 4M + P) / 6."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Planning Poker: A consensus-based technique often used in Agile teams, utilizing story points to estimate test design and execution effort."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Case Point (UCP) Method: Estimates testing effort based on actors, use cases, and technical/environmental complexity factors."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Best Practices for Manual Test Management"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Involve QA early in requirement analysis sessions to catch ambiguities before coding begins."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regularly update the Test Plan as project requirements evolve."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Factor in buffer time (roughly 20-30%) in test estimations for unexpected blockers, environment downtime, and defect re-testing."}]
